summary: TETFund's Academic Staff Training and Development (AST&D, also called TETFund Scholarship for Academic Staff, TSAS) pays for confirmed lecturers at Nigerian public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to do a Master's or PhD. Since 1 January 2025 the foreign component is suspended, so new awards are for study at other Nigerian universities (local), with occasional special partnership schemes. You do not apply to TETFund directly: your own institution nominates you through its TETFund desk, and you sign a bond to return and serve.
lookfor: You are a full-time, confirmed academic staff member of a TETFund beneficiary institution
A current admission letter to an NUC-approved Master's or PhD programme at another institution (not your employer)
Your department's justification that the degree fills a staffing need
You do not already hold the degree level you are seeking and are not on another scholarship
Medical fitness from a government hospital and a signed bond to return
Some institutions give preference to first- and second-generation academics; check your desk's call
cycle: There is no single national deadline. Each institution's TETFund desk issues its own call (often January–May) based on its yearly allocation; for example UNIBEN's 2025/26 call closed 28 February 2025 and UNILAG issued a 2026 call. Ask your desk office now when the 2027 call is expected.

eligibility.q: Are you a full-time academic staff member (lecturer, researcher or instructor) of a public university, polytechnic or college of education that benefits from TETFund?
eligibility.no: AST&D is only for staff of beneficiary institutions. Students should look at NELFUND, state scholarships, PTDF or international awards.

eligibility.q: Has your appointment been confirmed (not on probation or contract)?
eligibility.no: Ask your Registry when you will be confirmed and apply in the first call after confirmation.

eligibility.q: Are you seeking a degree level you do not already have (no second Master's or second PhD)?
eligibility.no: TETFund does not fund a second degree at the same level. Consider TETFund conference or research grants instead.

eligibility.q: Will you study at a different institution from your employer, in Nigeria?
eligibility.no: TETFund does not sponsor staff at their own institution. Foreign study is suspended for new awards since January 2025, so choose an NUC-approved programme elsewhere in Nigeria (or watch for special partnership calls).

eligibility.q: Is the programme full-time and on campus (not online or part-time)?
eligibility.no: Online and part-time programmes are not supported. Choose a full-time route.

eligibility.q: Are you free of any other scholarship for the same degree?
eligibility.no: You must give up the other award or not use TETFund for this degree.

eligibility.q: Are you willing to sign a bond to return and serve your institution after the programme?
eligibility.no: The bond is compulsory. If you plan to leave your job, look at other funding.

steps.title: Confirm you qualify and learn the current rules
steps.why: Rules changed in 2025: foreign study is suspended. Planning around old rules wastes months.
do: Answer every eligibility question above.
Open tetfund.gov.ng and read the FAQ, which confirms foreign scholarships are suspended.
Read one recent institutional call (e.g. UNILAG 2026 or UNIBEN 2025/26) to see the usual document list.
Write down: the degree you need, the field, and why your department needs it.
tips: If you hoped to study abroad, look also at Commonwealth, DAAD and university-funded studentships, and keep TETFund as the local route.
avoid: Relying on blog posts from before 2025 that describe foreign TETFund scholarships as open.
check: I know foreign study is not currently available for new awards

links.t: TETFund official website (FAQ on foreign scholarship suspension)
Channels TV: TETFund suspends foreign scholarship (Nov 2024)

steps.title: Visit your institution's TETFund desk office
steps.why: Your institution, not you, nominates candidates to TETFund. The desk office knows this year's allocation, deadline and forms.
do: Find your TETFund Desk Officer (often in Academic Planning or the Directorate of Research).
Ask: When is the next AST&D call? How many slots does our institution have? What documents are required? Is there an internal ranking?
Ask for the current nomination form and bond form, or the link to download them.
Ask how your institution ranks candidates (e.g. department need, years of service, first-generation preference).
tips: Get on the desk's mailing list or WhatsApp group so you see the internal call the day it is released.
avoid: Waiting for a national advert — there usually isn't one.
check: I know the expected call date and the document list

links.t: TETFund resources — downloads (AST&D Nomination Form listed)

steps.title: Get your Head of Department on board
steps.why: Most calls require a departmental justification letter signed by the HOD and Dean. Without it you will not be nominated.
do: Book a short meeting with your HOD.
Explain the degree you plan, the field, and the gap it fills (e.g. courses lacking PhD-holders, accreditation needs).
Ask them to support you in the department's staff development plan.
Ask when they can sign the justification letter.
tips: Bring a one-page note with the accreditation or staffing need — HODs sign faster when the case is written for them.
avoid: Choosing a field unrelated to what you teach.

steps.title: Choose the programme and host university
steps.why: The host must have an NUC-approved programme and cannot be your employer. A good fit also makes admission faster.
do: List 2–3 Nigerian universities with an NUC-approved Master's or PhD in your field.
For PhD, find a likely supervisor whose research matches your topic and email them a short introduction.
Check each programme's full-time study rules, fees schedule and admission timetable.
Confirm the programme length fits TETFund limits (PhD up to 3 years; Master's up to 2 years locally).
tips: Ask current TETFund scholars at your institution which hosts process admission and fee schedules quickly.
avoid: Picking a programme that does not issue a clear fee schedule — TETFund needs the fees stated.
check: I have a target programme and (for PhD) a willing supervisor

links.t: UNILAG 2026 AST&D call (example of an internal call)

steps.title: Write your research proposal (PhD) or concept note
steps.why: Postgraduate schools use the proposal to admit you and assign a supervisor; some TETFund desks also ask for supervisor and project details.
do: Check the host university's postgraduate school for its proposal format and length.
Write: title; background and problem; aims and objectives; brief literature review; methods; expected outcomes; work plan by semester; references.
Show a realistic 3-year timeline that fits TETFund's limit.
Ask your proposed supervisor to comment before you submit.
tips: Link your topic to a national or local need and to the courses you teach — it helps both the admission and your HOD's justification.
avoid: A topic too broad for 3 years.
Methods that need equipment the host does not have.
check: My proposal follows the host's format

links.t: YouTube: how to write a PhD research proposal

steps.prompt: Host university's research proposal: problem, objectives, methods, expected outcomes and work plan.
steps.limit: Set by the host postgraduate school — check its guidance

steps.title: Apply for admission and get a valid admission letter
steps.why: The admission letter is required and must be recent: one university's rules say not older than 12 months for PhD and 6 months for Master's.
do: Buy the host university's postgraduate form on its official website and complete it.
Upload transcripts, certificates, proposal and referee details as requested.
Follow up with the postgraduate school until the admission letter is issued.
Make sure the letter states the programme, start date and fees (or get a separate fee schedule).
tips: Time your admission so it is fresh when your institution's call opens.
avoid: Submitting an admission letter that has expired under your desk's rules.
check: My admission letter shows programme, start date and fees

links.t: Watch: Prof Faluyi on OAU Staff Applying and Accessing TETFund Grants (Obafemi Awolowo University)

steps.title: Get your medical fitness report
steps.why: TETFund calls require a medical fitness certificate from a government (public) hospital.
do: Go to a federal or state government hospital (often your institution's medical centre can refer you).
Ask for a medical fitness examination for scholarship purposes.
Pay the fee, complete the tests, and collect the signed and stamped report.
Scan it as PDF.
tips: Ask for the report on hospital letterhead with the doctor's name and stamp.
avoid: Private clinic reports — they may be rejected.
check: I have a signed government-hospital fitness report

steps.title: Assemble the full nomination pack
steps.why: Desk offices reject incomplete packs; most ask for both hard and soft copies.
do: Fill the TETFund AST&D nomination form neatly.
Collect: admission letter; fee schedule; HOD/Dean justification letter; letter of confirmation of appointment; current CV; copies of certificates; medical report; passport photo; bank details.
Print and sign two bond forms (UNILAG's 2026 call asked for two).
Scan everything as clear PDFs (photo as JPEG) and name files clearly.
Make two hard-copy sets.
tips: Use your institutional email if your desk requires it (UNIBEN did).
avoid: Mismatched names across documents — fix them with an affidavit or change-of-name notice first.
check: Every item on my desk's list is in both hard and soft copy

links.t: UNIBEN TETFund scholarship call 2025/2026 (document list example)

steps.title: Write a short CV and covering letter
steps.why: Internal committees rank nominees. A clear CV showing teaching load and research helps them justify you.
do: Update your CV: appointment dates, rank, courses taught, publications, service roles.
Write a one-page application letter to the officer named in the call (e.g. DVC Academic or Director of Academic Planning).
In the letter, state the degree, host, start date, and how it helps your department.
Ask a senior colleague to read both.
tips: Mention accreditation or teaching gaps your degree will fill.
avoid: Long letters — one page is enough.
check: CV and letter are complete and proofread
steps.prompt: Application letter: degree, host, start date, and the department need it meets.
steps.limit: About one page (no official limit — check your desk's call)

steps.title: Submit to your institution before its deadline
steps.why: Late submissions miss the batch your institution sends to TETFund.
do: Submit the hard copies to the office named in the call and the soft copies to the stated email or portal.
Get an acknowledgement (stamped copy or email reply).
Ask when the internal selection meeting will hold.
tips: Submit a week early so the desk can flag missing items in time.
avoid: Sending documents through a third party without a receipt.

steps.title: Follow nomination and TETFund approval
steps.why: After internal selection, your institution submits nominees to TETFund for approval and fund release; this can take months.
do: Check your institution's notices for the list of approved beneficiaries.
If approved, open or confirm the bank account needed for disbursement.
Collect your approval letter and keep copies.
Start the programme on the stated date.
tips: Stay polite and in touch with the desk office; ask for updates monthly, not daily.
avoid: Paying anyone who claims they can speed up approval.

links.t: TETFund TERAS platform (used by institutions to access interventions)

steps.title: Keep your bond and reporting duties
steps.why: Beneficiaries must submit yearly progress reports, and PhD scholars send their thesis to TETFund. Breaking the bond can mean repaying the money.
do: Submit a yearly progress report signed by your supervisor through your desk office.
Finish within the approved duration.
On completion, submit your thesis (PDF and hard copy for PhD) and return to your post.
Serve for the period stated in your bond.
tips: Keep a folder of all reports and letters; you may need them for promotion.
avoid: Abandoning the programme or not returning — abscondment is one reason foreign awards were suspended.
check: I know my bond term and reporting dates

faq.q: Can I still use TETFund to study abroad?
faq.a: Not for new awards. TETFund suspended the foreign component from 1 January 2025; scholars already abroad continue. Watch for special partnership calls sent through your institution.

faq.q: Do I apply on the TETFund website?
faq.a: No. You apply through your own institution's TETFund desk, which nominates you to TETFund.
It varies by institution and year. One university's 2023 call listed ₦1.5m a year for sciences and ₦1.2m for other fields; check your desk's current rates.

faq.q: Can I study at my own university?
faq.a: No. TETFund does not sponsor staff at their employing institution.

faq.q: Are polytechnic and college of education staff eligible?
faq.a: Yes, if your institution is a TETFund beneficiary and you meet the rules. Ask your desk office.
